evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Astrometry.net solving success and Gaia DR3 positional residuals provide an external, objective measurement of the recovered WCS solutions, independent of the detector's training labels.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: The headline outcome is astrometric recovery of previously failed plates via Astrometry.net blind solving and positional residuals against epoch-propagated Gaia DR3 coordinates, plus throughput measurements.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Supervised training and fine-tuning use bounding-box and class labels generated by SExtractor detections cross-matched with Gaia DR3, including the Gaia-guided target-domain labels built from initially solved UBAI plates.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported claims closely match the empirical evidence, showing that Plate-YOLO accelerates source extraction compared to SExtractor, achieves high calibration recovery on severely degraded plates, and yields comparable or slightly improved astrometric RMS residuals.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The evaluation combines component ablations on the source archive, cross-archive zero-shot and fine-tuned astrometric recovery on 150 previously failed UBAI plates (achieving 146/150 recovered), detection completeness and purity analyses, and astrometric residual comparisons relative to external Gaia DR3 coordinates across 500 plates.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Final plate calibration success via Astrometry.net and independent positional residual calculations (RMS relative to epoch-propagated Gaia DR3 coordinates) corroborate the object detection performance.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Astrometric blind solving success and WCS coordinate registration residuals against external Gaia DR3 catalog coordinates, along with processing throughput measurements.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Supervised training using ground-truth bounding box regression and classification labels generated by SExtractor detections cross-matched with Gaia DR3 catalogs on historical plate collections.

primary.limitations: The authors document residual dependency on reference catalog depth, sensitivity degradation for the faintest sources, failure on extended comet plates with trailed stars, and caution that instrumental magnitude rank correlations do not constitute calibrated photometry.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is comprehensively described, integrating architecture adjustments into YOLOv5 for micro-scale point sources, an objective Gaia-cross-matched pseudo-labeling strategy, and an instrumental brightness proxy for ranking detections before passing them to Astrometry.net.
primary.quality_rationale: The work provides a well-executed domain adaptation and detection pipeline that solves a concrete problem in historical astronomical archive preservation, backed by sound ablation studies and solid independent validation via Gaia DR3 astrometric calibration.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces Plate-YOLO, an end-to-end object detector combining source detection and stellar classification tailored for degraded historical astronomical photographic plates using Space-to-Depth modules, SimAM attention, a micro-scale P2 head, Normalized Wasserstein Distance loss, and a cross-archive fine-tuning strategy.
